overview:
Maven is a global knowledge marketplace and microconsulting platform founded in 2008 by Wyatt Nordstrom and Mark Platosh. Deliberately positioning itself beyond the traditional 'expert network' label, Maven operates as a self-service platform connecting knowledge seekers with 1M+ experts across 200+ countries — making it one of the largest expert databases in the industry alongside GLG and Guidepoint.

Maven's core differentiator is accessibility. While premium expert networks charge $1,000+ per call, Maven starts at $150 for a 30-minute consultation with no long-term contracts. This pay-as-you-go model appeals to SMBs, startups, consulting firms, and budget-conscious research teams. The company also offers unlimited subscription access for up to $30,000.

Beyond expert calls, Maven has evolved into three interconnected businesses: (1) the expert marketplace for consultations, surveys, and consulting projects; (2) a leading B2B and Healthcare Professional (HCP) sample provider for market research firms, known for the highest-quality B2B/HCP sample with removal rates an order of magnitude below industry average; and (3) a white-label consultant management platform that enables organizations to build private, custom expert networks integrated with their HRM/CRM systems.

Notable clients include Pepsi, IBM, NASA, Siemens, and Sanofi. Maven generates an estimated $5-10M in annual revenue.

history.narrative:
Wyatt Nordstrom (CEO/Chairman) and Mark Platosh co-founded Maven around 2008, with Anthony J. D'Alessandro also listed as a co-founder. The company built what it calls the 'world's largest consultant referral network' — a proprietary peer referral system where experts recruit other experts, enabling organic network growth to 1M+ professionals without the massive recruiting teams required by traditional expert networks.

Maven raised its first funding — $1M from Accel and angel investors — in 2010, followed by $2M from SuRo Capital in 2012. The company completed its Series A in January 2017, bringing total funding to approximately $3-8M (sources vary). Rather than pursuing aggressive venture-backed growth, Maven has operated relatively lean, building a sustainable business across expert calls, B2B sample, and enterprise platform services.

servicesDetailed.name: Expert Interviews (IDIs)
servicesDetailed.description: One-on-one phone/video consultations with experts, starting at $150/30 minutes. Includes call recording and machine transcription. AI-powered search, no long-term contracts. Pay-as-you-go or unlimited subscription models.

servicesDetailed.name: Electronic Surveys
servicesDetailed.description: Quantitative and qualitative surveys from targeted expert panels in a double-blinded environment. Used for market assessment, product feedback, competitive landscaping, and opinion gathering.

servicesDetailed.name: Client Discovery Program (CDP)
servicesDetailed.description: Two-part methodology combining a survey with private calls to source ideal purchase decision-makers and generate intelligence reports on pain points. Priced $25,000-$108,000.

servicesDetailed.name: B2B & Healthcare Professional Sample
servicesDetailed.description: Professional audiences including licensed HCPs for market research firms' studies. Known for the highest-quality B2B/HCP sample with removal rates an order of magnitude below industry average. HIPAA, Sunshine Act, and FCPA compliant.

servicesDetailed.name: Consultant Management Platform (White-Label)
servicesDetailed.description: SaaS platform for creating custom, private expert networks. Integrates with HRM/CRM systems. Enables internal knowledge sharing and external expert sourcing through the OpenTalent model.

servicesDetailed.name: Consulting Projects & Expert Panels
servicesDetailed.description: Task one or more experts with specific deliverables for hours to months. Also offers moderated group discussions bringing together multiple experts on a topic.

servicesDetailed.name: Staffing & Recruiting
servicesDetailed.description: Source professionals for part-time, temporary, or full-time roles through the expert network. 15% fee on first-year compensation for permanent placements.

aiPlatform.narrative: Maven is technology-first with AI-powered expert matching that analyzes requests and continuously improves match quality. The platform's most distinctive technology is its proprietary peer referral system — described as the world's largest consultant referral network — which grows the expert database organically. The referral commission system pays 10% ongoing bonus for first-year referral earnings, 50% one-time commission for specific inquiry referrals, and 40% client discounts when referred experts consult with colleagues. This creates a viral growth loop that built the 1M+ expert network without traditional recruiting overhead.

complianceExtended.narrative: Maven maintains compliance controls appropriate for its diverse client base spanning corporate, healthcare, and investment research. The platform is particularly strong in healthcare compliance, with features designed for HIPAA, Sunshine Act, FCPA, and debarment screening — critical for HCP (Healthcare Professional) engagements. Maven is self-certified under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, UK Extension, and Swiss-U.S. Data Privacy Framework.

complianceExtended.regulatoryContext: Maven serves a broad client base including healthcare/pharma companies requiring HIPAA compliance and investment firms needing MNPI controls. The self-service model places some compliance responsibility on clients. EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework certified. No evidence of SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certification. Clean regulatory record.

clientFit.narrative: Maven is ideal for organizations that want expert network access without premium pricing or long-term commitments. The self-service model, transparent pricing, and pay-as-you-go structure make it the most accessible expert network for SMBs, startups, and budget-conscious research teams. Maven's HCP sample business also makes it a key partner for market research firms. However, teams with growing institutional needs often 'graduate' to larger networks like GLG or Third Bridge.
